title: The soul enjoys scent (Berakhot 43b)
hook: a blessing over fragrance, the pleasure the soul enjoys, not the body
tomorrow: why would a man bless the road where a lion jumped him?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bless before taking: the earth is the LORD's before the blessing, and ours after it. Today the week comes back, and one more blessing, for something you can't eat.

A grandparent's coat in the closet still smells like them, years later, and one breath of it can undo a whole afternoon. Nobody gets full from that. Nothing is eaten. So what does the soul enjoy that the body doesn't? The Talmud answers in one word: scent.
screen: `A COAT IN THE CLOSET.` → `NOTHING EATEN.` → `THE SOUL'S PLEASURE: SCENT.`

segments.voice: The sages want a source for blessing a good smell, and they find it in the closing line of Psalm 150: "Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD." The Hebrew word there for breath, neshamah, is also a word for soul. So they ask: what does the soul enjoy, and not the body? That's scent. Food is shared by body and soul. A fragrance is the soul's alone, so it gets its own blessing. You can hear it at the end of every Shabbat, when a family passes a box of spices hand to hand and blesses its smell. And notice how this week was built. Chanina ben Dosa kept praying with a snake at his heel. Rabbi Chanina left one thing in our hands, awe. Moses prayed long, and short. A prayer flowed in the mouth. The returners stood higher. And the earth changed hands with a blessing. A whole week of the body teaching the soul: feet that didn't move, a mouth, a bowed head, a bite. Today it's just a breath in.
screen: `EVERY THING THAT HATH BREATH.` · `NESHAMAH: BREATH, AND SOUL.` · `THE SPICE BOX, HAND TO HAND.` · `A WEEK OF THE BODY.` · then, large: `THE SOUL ENJOYS SCENT.`

segments.voice: Find something with a good smell: a spice from the kitchen, a cut orange, a flower, soap. Hold it close and breathe it in slowly, more than once. If you know a blessing for fragrance, say it; if not, let the breath itself be the thanks.
screen: `SOMETHING THAT SMELLS GOOD.` · `BREATHE IT IN, SLOWLY.` · `THE BREATH IS THE THANKS.`

segments.voice: The soul enjoys scent: the pleasure the body doesn't share, blessed because every thing that has breath praises.
From the spice box: the soul enjoys scent, even when nothing is eaten. A week of Berakhot, complete.
